text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The disorganised nature of elections in the centre-right Democratic Party forced a cancellation of their results at the party's congress in Limassol yesterday.

- The United Nations secretary-general will decide whether to call the leaders of the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities to direct talks following contacts under secretary-general Kieran Prendergast is due to have in Cyprus this week.
- Elections are cancelled in the Democratic Party.
- Glafcos Clerides will be voted out of the presidency if opposition parties unite, says communist Akel party chief Demetris Christofias.
- The United Nations plans three rounds of direct talks on Cyprus by September. Security and Cyprus's accession to the European Union will be on the agenda of the first round.
- The International Labour Office proposes an increase in employees and employers contributions to the social security fund.
- Elections in the Democratic Party will probably be held at the weekend after the cancellation of the first round yesterday.
- The funeral is due to be held today of a 12-year-old boy who drowned when the fishing boat he was in with his father and another man began leaking. The third man is still missing at sea.
